summary: Return all start indices of substrings of s that are anagrams of p.
mainInsight: An anagram window has exactly len(p) characters with the same counts as p. Maintain counts relative to p: decrement as characters enter and, when a count goes negative (too many), shrink from the left; a window of size len(p) with no negatives is an anagram.

promptVariants: In your solution cnt starts as the counts of p. What does cnt[c] represent while the window slides, and what does cnt[c] < 0 mean?
Explain the meaning of the count array in the variable-window version.
cards.answer: cnt[c] = how many more copies of c the window still needs to match p. Entering a character decrements it; a negative value means the window contains too many c's, so we move l (re-incrementing) until it is 0 again. When the window has len(p) characters and no negative counts it matches p exactly.
cards.explanation: The window never exceeds len(p) because overflow is removed immediately.

cards.explanation: Each character enters and leaves the window at most once.

promptVariants: Why can the `while cnt[toIdx(c)] < 0` loop pop several characters, and what does `r - l + 1 == len(p)` confirm?
Why does this also handle characters of s that do not appear in p?
cards.answer: A new character that exceeds its allowance forces the left edge to advance past the earlier copy of that character, possibly removing several others on the way. If the window then has exactly len(p) characters and no count is negative, the counts equal p's. A character not in p starts at 0, goes to -1 and shrinks the window all the way past itself (empty window).
keyPoints: Shrink until the count is restored
Size == len(p) with no negatives => anagram
